design.oneDeclaredScopeMap: FLOOR_RAIL_COUNTY_SCOPES in src/lib/publish-readiness-gate.mjs: { maxImperviousCoverPct: { counties: ['48453'], ruling: '<the engine #444 citation, naming 48453>' } }.
invariantsEnforcedAtModuleLoadAndInTests: every key must be a member of PUBLISH_FLOOR_RAIL_KEYS (a scope entry for a rail that is not on the floor throws)
counties must be a non-empty array of 5-digit FIPS strings
ruling must be a non-empty string

EVERY county in an entry's list must be named literally in that entry's ruling -- so widening a scope is mechanically impossible without rewriting the ruling that authorises it (the dispatch's fourth test, made a load-time invariant rather than a promise)
design.countyAwareFloor: floorRailsForCounty(requiredRails, countyFips) splits the requested floor into { required, skipped, scopedUndecided }. A rail with no scope entry is always required. A scoped rail is required in its scope counties, listed in skippedByScope outside them, and -- when the county cannot be determined at all -- lands in scopedUndecided, which makes the gate refuse RAIL_SCOPE_UNMEASURED rather than guess. An absent county is never read as 'in scope' (which would silently drop a floor rail) and never as 'out of scope' (which would silently widen it).
design.countyResolution: explicit countyFips from requirePreBakeReadiness wins; otherwise the county is read from the parcel_gate_verdict rows themselves (PRE_BAKE_READINESS_SQL already selects county_fips on every row). Rows naming more than one county, or naming a county other than the caller's, refuse RAIL_SCOPE_UNMEASURED -- two numbers that should agree and do not.
design.verdictUntouched: No cell and no verdict is written or changed. requirePreBakeReadiness keeps querying the FULL floor (the SQL params are unchanged, which the existing test at test/publish.test.mjs:2185 pins), so the skipped rail's stored verdict -- an honest 'refuse' with its count under P-252 -- is carried in the summary and stays visible in parcel_gate_verdict.
design.summaryShape: { ok, checked (every rail the floor names, unchanged semantics), countyFloorRails (what THIS county must meet), skippedByScope [{ rail, counties, ruling, verdict, unaccountedCount }], verdicts [{ rail, verdict, unaccountedCount, requiredForCounty }] }. The skip names its ruling, so the record shows a ruled scope limit rather than a silent pass.
design.recordingTheSkip: #157's dispatch falsifier 3 bounds the diff to 'the gate module and tests'. Mission item 3 requires that a PUBLISH RECORD show the skip, and the publish record is built by bastrop-publish.mjs recordReadinessEvent, which copies named fields out of the summary. So falsifier 3's file bound is AMENDED here, before writing anything, to 'the gate module, the one recording line that carries the summary into run_events, and tests' -- one added field, no logic change, no store write. Declared rather than done quietly; if the planner prefers the narrower bound, drop that one line and the skip is visible only to the caller, not in run_events.
